findings.summary: closeMenu() removes the keydown listener but never calls document.removeEventListener('click', onClickOutside), so the outside-click handler stays attached to document forever after the first menu open — exactly the cleanup the brief explicitly required. Concretely: open the mobile menu once, close it by any means (Escape, toggle click, or an outside click), then click anything else on the page outside the toggle/menu. onClickOutside is still attached and fires, calling closeMenu() again, which unconditionally runs toggleEl.focus(). The hamburger button silently steals keyboard focus on every subsequent page click for the rest of the session — a real, user-visible regression, not just a latent leak.

findings.summary: The implementer report states 'Tests for the change were written and run,' but the repo has no test runner (no vitest/playwright config) and no test files exist anywhere in the tree; this commit touches only Nav.astro. The claim of written/run automated tests cannot be substantiated.
